title: Weighted Graph
body:
A [[Graph]] whose edges carry a number: distance, cost, capacity, latency, whatever the
graph is modelling. Without weights the only question you can ask is "is there a path"; with
them you can ask "what is the *cheapest* path", which is where the interesting graph
algorithms start.

```
A --5-- B
|      /
2    1
| /
C --3-- D
```

Storing them is a small change to either representation: an [[Adjacency Matrix]] holds the
weight in the cell instead of a boolean (with 0 or infinity meaning "no edge"), and an
[[Adjacency List]] holds (neighbour, weight) pairs instead of bare neighbours.

Weights can be combined with direction: a [[Directed Graph]] with weights is the usual model
for road networks, where A to B and B to A need not cost the same.

Two classic problems live here. **Shortest path** (Dijkstra's algorithm, which repeatedly
takes the nearest unvisited vertex out of a [[Heap]]) and **[[Minimum Spanning Tree]]**
(Kruskal's or Prim's, connecting every vertex for the least total weight). Neither is
covered in this course; [[ALGORITHMS AND COMPLEXITY]] takes them.
